entry.title: FlowReconBench: Accuracy, calibration and cost of learned and classical flow reconstruction from sparse sensors
entry.summary: Reconstructing full flow fields from sparse sensors requires prior assumptions about unmeasured regions and physical variables. Yet it remains unclear when learned models outperform classical estimators and which aspects of their predictions can be trusted. FlowReconBench evaluates ten learned and five classical methods on three regimes: a laminar cylinder wake across Reynolds numbers, two-dimensional Kolmogorov turbulence and a large-scale three-dimensional (3D) isotropic turbulence. Methods share leakage-controlled splits and sensor draws and are scored on per-channel error, ensemble spread, calibration, spectra and cost. The leading method changes for each regime. Classical methods perform strongly in low-order and dense-sensing regimes. On the cylinder wake, linear stochastic estimation and gappy proper orthogonal decomposition lead, including for unobserved pressure. In 3D, inverse-distance weighting matches the best learned methods on observed channels. Data-driven methods become superior at decreasing sensor density or poor sensor observability. On Kolmogorov flow, continuous ranked probability score and error yield different method rankings: generative models offer broader but underdispersed ensembles, while deterministic models prioritize pointwise error. Generative models balance this tradeoff through their sampler budget, with a larger budget improving ensemble quality at higher computational cost. In 3D, scaling tests demonstrate that queryable methods are flat in memory, while full-grid construction methods run out of memory. Observing only 2 of 4 fields leaves the problem kinematically underconstrained, yet a latent model can reproduce structural similarities to the ground truth.
entry.arxiv:comment: 18 pages, 7 figures, 8 tables. Supplementary material (16 pages, 2 figures, 5 tables) is included as an ancillary file

entry.title: Sublinear multi-type preferential attachment
entry.summary: We consider a random growing graph model with two \emph{types}, or \emph{communities}, that belongs to the class of preferential attachment models. Starting from an initial graph $G_0$ in which each node has a type, the graph $G_{n+1}$ is generated by addition of a new node, which attaches through an edge to a node $v$ of $G_n$. The probability of attaching to $v$ depends on the communities of both the new node and $v$, and is proportional to $\operatorname{deg}_n(v)^γ$, where $γ\in[0, 1]$. We establish a convergence result for the limiting proportion of vertices of each degree and in each community in a certain regime of the parameter $γ$. To this end, we first use stochastic approximation techniques to reduce the convergence problem to the study of a non-linear evolution equation. We then use a probabilistic coupling approach to investigate the long-time behavior of the unique solution to this evolution equation. We emphasize that the techniques previously used to handle the single-community case cannot be extended directly to our setting. Indeed, the associated continuous-time embedding is not a multitype branching process in the usual sense, since the transition rates at any given time $t$ depend on the entire graph structure at that time.

entry.title: Human Mobility Sensing Using Wall-Reflected Beamformed Millimeter-Wave Communication Signals
entry.summary: Existing millimeter-wave (mmWave) communication beam patterns spatially weight human-scattered signals and shape the received-power signatures induced by human motion. We exploit these beam-shaped signatures for device-free walkingpace and walk-direction classification using a wall-reflected 60.8-GHz link with closely spaced phased arrays and fixed communication beamforming vectors. Human movement alters the interference between wall-reflected and scattered signals, producing power oscillations surrounding a central blockage fade. A beam-dependent interference model provides a physical interpretation of these signatures. Using received-power statistics from a continuous-tone experiment, we extract fade duration for walking-pace classification and pre/post-fade asymmetries for walk-direction classification. Measurements comprise 144 crossings from three participants along perpendicular and diagonal trajectories. Under leave-one-participant-out validation, logistic regression achieves 86.1% binary and 79.2% three-class walking pace accuracy, and 77.1% travel-direction accuracy. The results demonstrate mobility sensing using fixed communication beams without channel estimation, Doppler processing, or dedicated radar hardware

entry.title: Joint Association and Beamforming Design for Cooperative ISAC Systems
entry.summary: Cooperation among multiple base stations (BSs) improves both communication and sensing in integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) networks. However, it requires deciding which BSs serve each communication user (CU) and each target, and how each BS beamforms. In this work, we consider joint BS-CU and BS-target association, and beamforming for a general cooperative ISAC system, overcoming prior simplifications such as single-user or target setups, fixed BS roles, coherent radar or separate waveforms. We maximize a joint communication rate and position Cramer-Rao lower bound (CRLB) based tradeoff utility while guaranteeing a minimum service per-CU using a data queue model. We develop a successive convex approximation (SCA)-based beamforming with closed-form updates. The discrete association problem is solved as an overarching layer using a low-complexity algorithm. Numerical results validate the effectiveness of the algorithm and unveil benefits of cooperative communication and sensing.

entry.title: Improper Signaling for Clutter-Limited Angle Estimation in ISAC
entry.summary: Integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) transmit designs typically optimize the transmit covariance under proper signaling, leaving the potential sensing benefits of pseudo-covariance unexplored. This paper investigates the conditions under which transmit pseudo-covariance can influence the angle Cramer-Rao bound (CRB) of a deterministic target in the presence of clutter. For a prescribed transmit covariance and a single clutter patch, we establish that CRB sensitivity occurs if and only if the clutter is illuminated, exhibits nonzero non-circularity, and overlaps the angle-informative component of the target response. This characterization demonstrates that angular separation alone does not determine whether transmit impropriety can improve sensing performance. We derive a closed-form optimal incident-field pseudo-variance that minimizes the angle CRB over the set of feasible transmit pseudo-covariances. Under fully non-circular clutter scattering, the optimal design eliminates the clutter-induced CRB penalty. Numerical results for a 32-antenna ISAC system show CRB reductions of up to 99% relative to proper sensing under complete overlap and 30% under partial overlap, as well as up to approximately 7 dB lower clutter-induced CRB penalty across target-clutter separations. These findings identify transmit pseudo-covariance as a conditional sensing design resource whose effectiveness depends on clutter statistics and projected target-clutter geometry.
entry.arxiv:comment: 6 pages, 4 figures, submitted to the IEEE International Conference on Communications (ICC), 2027

entry.title: Integrated Identity Protection for Semantic Communications in Embodied IoT Systems
entry.summary: Embodied Internet of Things (IoT) systems are promoting the adoption of task-oriented semantic communication (SemCom), in which the trustworthy task decisions require both semantic information reliability and source legitimacy. However, existing trustworthy designs in SemCom mainly focus on semantic content recovery and protection, with limited attention to source legitimacy. Motivated by this limitation, this paper establishes a new information exploitation paradigm for integrated SemCom-identity protection to address active source impersonation and passive identity inference by treating each SemCom signal as an inherent carrier of both task-relevant semantic information and transmitter physical identity information. We first examine these two information resources and then analyze their integration feasibility at the observation, processing, and decision levels. To exploit these resources for trustworthy decision making, we further develop a dual-branch identity protection mechanism under different operating modes. In the authentication mode, semantic recovery and physical-layer source verification are performed in parallel using the same received observation. In the concealment mode, identity exposure is suppressed while semantic recovery quality is maintained to support anonymous sensing reports. The resulting outputs are jointly interpreted to support task decisions under mode-specific identity protection requirements. Finally, two representative case studies on active source impersonation and passive identity inference are presented to evaluate the proposed framework.

entry.title: Fundamental Limits of Coherent Imaging in The Presence of Atmospheric Turbulence
entry.summary: We study the fundamental limits of jointly estimating the signal amplitude and the atmospheric phase distortion in complex-valued multi-look coherent imaging, where the measurements are corrupted by multiplicative speckle and additive Gaussian noise, all looks share a known Gaussian sensing matrix, and both parameters belong to structured classes. By analyzing a constrained maximum likelihood estimator, we establish an upper bound on the joint minimax risk that holds uniformly over the admissible parameter classes, while oracle reductions and Fano-type arguments yield worst-case lower bounds over the admissible parameter classes. These results quantify the effects of structural complexity, signal and measurement dimensions, the number of looks, and the noise level, and establish matching minimax rates in several settings, with a remaining gap for phase estimation at low noise when the measurement dimension exceeds the signal dimension. We also construct a two-stage estimator for signal recovery under arbitrary diagonal sign distortions in the real-valued analogue. Under additional conditions, it recovers the signs up to a global sign with high probability and yields a uniform signal risk bound without a distortion-complexity term. Numerical experiments illustrate the dependence of the joint, signal, and phase errors on the model parameters and provide further support for the theoretical analysis.

entry.title: Benchmarking Fine-Grained Visual Reasoning for Remote Sensing in Urban Management
entry.summary: Fine-grained visual reasoning is essential for remote sensing in urban management, yet remains underexplored in the evaluation of multimodal large language models (MLLMs). We introduce UMBench, a fine-grained urban remote sensing benchmark built from unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) images for multiple urban management tasks such as traffic monitoring, urban construction, environmental quality, and disaster warning. Evaluations on UMBench reveal that current MLLMs often rely on scene-level priors and overlook fine-grained visual evidence. To address this issue, we further propose a novel evidence-first chain-of-thought method that directs models to inspect fine-grained visual evidence in a training-free manner. Experiments show that our method can improve the performance of both open-source and commercial MLLMs on UMBench.
entry.arxiv:comment: Accepted by IEEE AP-GARSS 2026; 4 pages, 3 figures, 3 tables

entry.title: Dexterous Robotic Hands in the Foundation-Model Era: A Full-Stack Survey of Hardware, Data, Cross-Embodiment Transfer, Learning, and Evaluation
entry.summary: Dexterous robotic hands are increasingly coupled to large-scale human data and foundation models, yet progress in hardware, representation learning and evaluation is often assessed separately. This survey reviews work from January 2024 to early November 2026, with earlier studies included to establish technical lineages. We organize the literature into five interdependent layers: hardware; data collection and curation; cross-embodiment transfer; learning and foundation models; and evaluation and applications. Human hand-object understanding and tactile sensing provide two cross-cutting perspectives. A system-level architecture, comparative tables and five case analyses connect design choices across these layers. We distinguish within-study experimental comparisons from heterogeneous corpus statistics, vendor specifications and company-reported results. Three conclusions emerge. First, the value of human data depends on kinematic, visual and contact alignment, not recording volume alone. Second, shared action representations and foundation policies do not remove embodiment-specific constraints on force, latency and contact. Third, task completion is insufficient to establish physical correctness or deployment readiness. Evidence remains limited for zero-shot transfer of contact-rich skills between morphologically different hands, long-duration reliability, and cross-sensor tactile generalization. We identify eleven open problems and propose reporting interfaces and controlled comparisons that can make full-stack progress more measurable. The review is a structured narrative synthesis rather than a pooled performance ranking or an exhaustive systematic review.
entry.arxiv:comment: 45 pages, 8 figures, 21 tables. Structured narrative review of hardware, data, cross-embodiment transfer, foundation models, tactile sensing, and evaluation for dexterous robotic hands

entry.title: Combinatorial Boolean Matrix Multiplication in $n^3 / 2^{Ω(\sqrt{\log n})}$ Time
entry.summary: For over fifty years, combinatorial algorithms for Boolean matrix multiplication (BMM) and triangle detection saved only polylogarithmic factors over cubic time. At STOC 2024, Abboud, Fischer, Kelley, Lovett, and Meka broke this barrier with a deterministic $O(n^3 / 2^{Ω((\log n)^{1/7})})$-time algorithm, and asked whether $n^3 / 2^{Ω(\sqrt{\log n})}$ time is achievable. We answer this question in the affirmative, giving deterministic combinatorial algorithms for both BMM and triangle detection running in $O(n^3 / 2^{Ω(\sqrt{\log n})})$ time. Following Abboud et al., we decompose $(A,B)$ into pairs of submatrices $(A_k,B_k)$, called \emph{pieces}, each of which is either sparse or pseudorandom in a sense that forces $A_k\star B_k$ to be nearly all-ones on its vertex sets. Whereas their decomposition produces $2^{O(d^7)}$ pieces at regularity parameter $d$, we obtain $2^{O(d^2)}$ pieces, directly improving the runtime exponent from $(\log n)^{1/7}$ to $\sqrt{\log n}$. Prior work found pseudorandom pieces by repeatedly restricting to denser submatrices, paying worst-case vertex losses at each step that compounded across nested recursion levels, together with an expensive derandomization step. We eliminate the extra powers of $d$ by matching the vertex loss at each step to the size of its density jump so losses telescope across scales, derandomizing witness search via $L_d$-norm estimation so the sampler length stays $2^{O(d)}$, and bounding overlap across the recursion with a fractional density-weighted volume budget rather than raw submatrix volume.

entry.title: Adaptive Optics for the Extremely Large Telescope: overcoming Point Spread Function challenges with MORFEO
entry.summary: MORFEO is the multi-conjugate adaptive optics (MCAO) relay for the Extremely Large Telescope (ELT) of the European Southern Observatory. It combines the adaptive mirrors of the telescope (M4-M5) with two post-focal deformable mirrors to deliver a stable, diffraction-limited point spread function over a field approaching 1'. MORFEO senses the atmosphere using six sodium laser guide stars and up to three natural guide stars distributed across a $\sim$160'' technical field, enabling sky coverage levels of order 50% at the South Galactic Pole. Through its two gravity-invariant ports, MORFEO feeds the MICADO first-light imager and spectrograph with a corrected field of 51''and HARMONI, the high-angular resolution integral field spectrograph. SHARP, a concept for a multi-object near-infrared spectrograph at the ELT, adopts MORFEO as its reference MCAO architecture for evaluating achievable image quality and scientific performance. In this paper, we summarise the MCAO capabilities delivered by MORFEO, its optical quality, tomographic performance, stability of the corrected focal plane, and the accuracy of telemetry-based PSF reconstruction, and discuss their relevance for the development of SHARP and other wide-field spectroscopic concepts at the ELT.
entry.arxiv:comment: 21 pages, 5 figures, published on New Astronomy on Aug 2026

entry.title: When to Ask for Help: Uncertainty-Triggered Aerial Refinement for Off-Road Navigation
entry.summary: Heterogeneous air-ground teams can use aerial sensing to address the limited range and viewpoint of ground-vehicle sensors, but deciding when the UGV needs assistance and what information the UAV should collect remains a challenge. This paper presents a planner-conditioned air-ground assistance method that evaluates how uncertain map information affects the UGV's current MPPI rollouts. When navigation remains degraded, we score the same rollouts under resolved map hypotheses, select the map layer with the largest useful improvement, request the corresponding aerial measurement, fuse the returned information, and replan. Unlike approaches driven by fixed support roles, task structure, or uncertainty alone, our method conditions assistance on whether resolving uncertainty improves predicted ground navigation. Across 180 simulation trials on three off-road routes, the method achieves 98.9% goal attainment while reducing mean UAV flight time by 87.7% relative to continuous greedy aerial mapping. Aggregated across the routes, each second of estimated UAV flight time saves 2.94 s of UGV navigation time. Field experiments spanning approximately 2 km of UGV operation demonstrate uncertainty resolution and successful navigation recovery.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Driven Efficient Communication for UAV-Based Collaborative Perception
entry.summary: Unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV)-based collaborative perception enables multiple agents to share complementary perceptual information, overcoming limitations such as occlusion and limited sensing range. Communication efficiency is a critical bottleneck, as UAVs operate under stringent bandwidth and computational constraints. However, existing spatial selection methods focus predominantly on foreground regions to reduce missed detections, neglecting perceptually ambiguous regions and leaving false detections unresolved. We propose UCP, an uncertainty-driven framework that characterizes collaborative value through observational uncertainty, identifying sensor-limited regions, and discriminative uncertainty, capturing model-level ambiguity near the decision boundary. These estimates drive spatial request and supply maps for efficient inter-agent communication, and the received messages are aggregated via U-Fusion, an uncertainty-guided cross-attention module. Experiments on three benchmarks across 3D object detection and trajectory prediction demonstrate a superior performance-bandwidth trade-off with high interpretability and strong generalizability.

entry.title: Informing research priorities for distributed acoustic sensing: insights from a citizens' panel
entry.summary: This report presents findings from a Citizens' Panel convened by the SOUNDSCALE project (www.soundscale.ac.uk) to inform research priorities for distributed acoustic sensing (DAS). Across three online and in-person workshops, 48 residents from Hampshire and London explored the technology's potential uses, risks, governance, and societal implications. The report summarises their deliberations and priorities, and reflects on the challenges of involving citizens in early-stage research on an unfamiliar technology.

entry.title: TOP: Transmission-Oriented Remote Sensing Pansharpening
entry.summary: Pansharpening has been extensively studied as a fundamental image fusion task in remote sensing. However, most existing methods focus on improving fusion quality under the implicit assumption that high-resolution observations have already been fully downlinked to the ground. As a result, existing models are highly vulnerable to perturbations introduced by lossy compression used for downlink transmission. To address this limitation, we present, to the best of our knowledge, the first transmission oriented pansharpening (TOP) framework, which unifies compact latent coding, onboard pansharpening, and efficient downlink transmission within a single satellite-toground pipeline. TOP encodes remote-sensing observations into a compact binary latent space, where a lightweight onboard fusion module can efficiently predict the fused binary latent code. Since only the compact fused code is downlinked, the transmission payload is substantially reduced. Overall, TOP enables low-payload downlink and lightweight onboard processing while maintaining high fusion quality under severe bandwidth constraints. Experiments across multispectral and hyperspectral settings show that TOP consistently achieves superior fusion quality at higher compression ratios than representative pansharpening methods paired with standard lossy codecs. For example, on GaoFen-2, TOP attains a fusion PSNR of 31.4 dB at a downlink compression ratio of 50x. This design also points toward transmissionoriented processing for other remote-sensing tasks. The code will be made available at https://github.com/JingZe-Liang/TOP.git.
